What makes it RISC?

Instructions use regular fields, arithmetic stays register-to-register, and only explicit load/store instructions enter the data cache. The five pipeline stages can overlap across different instructions.

What is physically simplified?

A real core contains many more buffers, predictors, translation structures, clock trees, power domains, and millions of transistors. These models preserve instructional data flow rather than literal floorplanning.

Under the hood

Why they behave differently

Architecture is an engineering trade-off across instruction encoding, decoding hardware, memory access rules, pipeline scheduling, and code density—not a simple competition with a single winner.

01 · ENCODING

Instruction format

OPRDRS1RS2

RISC favors fixed-width 32-bit fields where register specifiers always sit in the same bit positions. CISC uses variable-length 1–15 byte encodings (prefixes, opcode, ModR/M, SIB, displacement, immediate) to pack more work into fewer program bytes.

02 · DATAPATH

Load–store vs memory operands

REG→ALU→MEM

A load–store RISC ISA isolates memory access inside explicit LW/SW instructions while arithmetic stays register-to-register. CISC instructions can combine address generation, cache access, and ALU arithmetic inside one architectural command.

03 · TRANSLATION

Hardwired decode vs microcode

Simple RISC commands map directly to pipeline control signals in a single cycle. Complex CISC commands are cracked by hardware decoders or a Microcode ROM sequencer into multiple internal RISC-like micro-operations (µops).

04 · PIPELINING

Hazards & forwarding

IFIDEXMEMWB

Overlapping instructions creates data hazards (RAW dependencies) and control hazards (branches). Processors resolve data hazards with ALU-to-ALU forwarding paths and handle branches via prediction and speculative execution.

05 · DYNAMIC EXECUTION

Renaming, scheduling & ROB

RENAME→SCHED→ROB

High-performance cores map architectural registers (`EAX`, `R1`) onto a larger pool of physical registers to eliminate false dependencies, execute ready micro-ops out of order, and commit results in program order through a Reorder Buffer (ROB).

06 · CONVERGENCE

Code density, CPI & modern CPUs

BYTES×INSTR×CPI

Total execution time equals Instructions × CPI × Clock Period. Fewer architectural instructions do not guarantee higher speed. Modern CISC chips use RISC-like internal micro-op engines, while modern RISC ISAs add compressed and vector extensions.

Knowledge check

Design is trade-off,
not a scoreboard.

Modern processors blur the historical line: many CISC cores translate instructions into RISC-like micro-ops, while RISC ISAs continue to add specialized extensions.
